23               ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator

25               SENATOR MARCHIONE:   Thank you, 


                                                                4470

 1  Mr. President.  

 2               Today I have the privilege of 

 3  introducing the 2015-2016 New York State Dairy 

 4  Princess, Stephanie McBath.  

 5               Stephanie was named New York State 

 6  Dairy Princess after competing earlier this year 

 7  against 22 county dairy princesses in a two-day 

 8  event.  

 9               She is a remarkable young woman who 

10  will be graduating from Schuylerville High School 

11  next week and going on to Cornell University this 

12  fall.  

13               She is the daughter of Julie and 

14  David McBath.  Also with her today is Bill Peck, 

15  who is the owner of a wonderful farm in 

16  Schuylerville where Stephanie keeps her farm 

17  animals.  And also with them is Mrs. Shultz.

18               The Dairy Princess program is 

19  sponsored by the American Dairy Association and 

20  Dairy Council and seeks to highlight the 

21  nutrition and importance of dairy products while 

22  also fostering a deeper appreciation of local 

23  dairy farmers within the community.  

24               In her role as the 2015-2016 

25  New York State Dairy Princess, Stephanie will 


                                                                4471

 1  serve as the primary spokesperson for New York's 

 2  dairy industry.  Her many responsibilities will 

 3  include making appearances at the all of the 

 4  county dairy princess contests.  

 5               Stephanie has been busy 

 6  representing the New York State dairy industry 

 7  since she was crowned Dairy Princess, and she has 

 8  a very eventful schedule ahead of her this 

 9  summer, including spending a great deal of time 

10  at the New York State Fair in Syracuse at the end 

11  of August and into September.  One of her duties 

12  there will be the unveiling of the traditional 

13  800-pound butter sculpture.  

14               In addition, Stephanie is looking 

15  forward to conducting numerous activities to help 

16  educate children and consumers about local dairy 

17  farmers and the benefits of dairy products.  

18               Stephanie has brought enduring 

19  honor to her family, her community and the dairy 

20  industry through her many achievements.  And now 

21  it is an honor for me to present to you Stephanie 

22  McBath, New York State 2015-2016 Dairy 

23  Princess -- if you'll please rise -- and her 

24  family and friends.

10               SENATOR FUNKE:   Thank you, 

11  Mr. President, for allowing me to explain my vote 

12  on this.  

13               When I began, I got a call from a 

14  constituent, Joy Getnick, who reached out to 

15  voice her strong support for the Child Health 

16  Plus program while suggesting recommendations on 

17  how to improve it.  

18               Joy explained to my staff a 

19  situation that both she and her friend came 

20  across while participating in Child Health Plus, 

21  and it was this.  The two had enrolled their 

22  soon-to-be-newborns in Child Health Plus prior to 

23  the children being born.  When they went to 

24  confirm their coverage, they were informed that 

25  the coverage didn't take effect until the first 


                                                                4534

 1  day of the following month, which left over a 

 2  two-week gap in coverage.  

 3               Due to the language of the law, 

 4  once enrolled, coverage could not take place 

 5  until the first day of the month following the 

 6  date of a presumed eligibility determination.  So 

 7  that created a coverage gap from the point of 

 8  application that could extend up to 30 days.  

 9               Having no insurance coverage for a 

10  newborn is a pretty scary situation that no 

11  parent wants to face.  So this bill corrects this 

12  dilemma by allowing families who sign up and are 

13  approved for Child Health Plus prior to or within 

14  60 days of their child's birth to have coverage 

15  take effect the day the child is born.

16               This bill is an important piece of 

17  legislation that's going to benefit many 

18  middle-class families across our state.  

19  Hopefully parents of newborns will be able to 

20  sleep a little bit sounder at night, assuming a 

21  parent of a newborn sleeps at all.  And I am 

22  proud to be sponsoring this bill, and I encourage 

23  my colleagues to vote in the affirmative.

24               Thank you, Mr. President.

 6               SENATOR SAVINO:   Thank you, 

 7  Mr. President.

 8               Last year in the budget this house, 

 9  joined by the Assembly and the Governor, decided 

10  to do something for seniors and the disabled in 

11  the City of New York when we increased the income 

12  eligibility for those who could apply for the 

13  Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption and the 

14  Disabled Rent Increase Exemption to an annual 

15  household income of $50,000.  Prior to that, it 

16  had been $29,000.  By that action we extended 

17  protection to thousands of more seniors and 

18  disabled in New York City.

19               That legislation that we adopted 

20  though, however, sunsets.  And this legislation 

21  that we're taking up today will not only restore 

22  that eligibility, but it will make it permanent, 

23  providing permanent relief for seniors and the 

24  disabled who are living in rental units in the 

25  City of New York.


                                                                4558

 1               On top of that, we also took it a 

 2  step further, because many of our seniors and 

 3  disabled are also homeowners.  They would not be 

 4  eligible for that protection, so we're expanding 

 5  the SHE and DHE program, which is the Senior 

 6  Citizen Homeowner's Exemption and Disabled 

 7  Homeowner's Exemption.  It would provide a 

 8  property tax exemption of up to 50 percent of the 

 9  assessed property value for seniors or disabled 

10  residents who own one-, two- or three-family 

11  homes, condominiums or cooperative apartments, 

12  and who will be at least 65 years of age in the 

13  year that they apply.

14               We are also taking a step today to 

15  correct a mistake by the City of New York -- I 

16  know my colleague Senator Comrie is going to 

17  speak about it.  He represents a constituent who 

18  faced a horror story recently.  

19               So I want to thank all of my 

20  colleagues for supporting the first time and 

21  supporting the permanentization of this benefit, 

22  which really does make a real difference in the 

23  lives of seniors and the disabled.  

24               Thank you, Mr. President.
